title: The relevance of SDG 7 to local communities
excerpt: SDG 7 is often talked about as a global target for other places. Looking closer, its promise of affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy is surprisingly local.
body:
Sustainable Development Goal 7 aims to *"ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all."* When I first read it, I filed it mentally under international development — something about electrification in other parts of the world. This week's readings made me realise how local it is.

## The targets, in plain language

- **7.1** — Everyone has access to affordable, reliable, modern energy services.
- **7.2** — A much larger share of energy comes from renewable sources.
- **7.3** — The rate of improvement in energy efficiency doubles.
- **7.a and 7.b** — Countries cooperate on research, investment and infrastructure, especially to support developing countries.

## Why it matters close to home

Even in wealthy countries, the four words *affordable, reliable, sustainable, modern* don't apply equally to everyone:

- **Affordable** — some households spend a large share of their income on heating and power. Energy poverty is real in cold climates.
- **Reliable** — rural and remote communities can face more frequent outages and longer restoration times.
- **Sustainable** — many remote communities in Canada are not connected to the main grid and still rely on diesel generators.
- **Modern** — older, poorly insulated homes lock people into high bills and discomfort.

Seen this way, SDG 7 isn't something that's "done" once a country has an electricity grid. It's a lens for asking who is still being left behind.

## What local action can look like

- Home energy retrofits targeted at households with the highest energy burden.
- Community-owned solar or wind projects that keep benefits local.
- Microgrids and storage to reduce diesel dependence in remote communities.
- Energy literacy programmes, so people can make informed choices.
- Local energy plans that connect housing, transport and economic development.

[[If relevant, add an example from your own community or home country here — local examples make this post much stronger.]]

## Key takeaways

> - SDG 7 is about everyone, everywhere — including communities in wealthy countries.
> - The four qualities in the goal give a practical checklist for local energy planning.
> - Local ownership and efficiency are two of the most direct ways to make progress.
